subject: Clarifying export windows and residency edge cases for audit/access logs
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@finvero.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Finvero Security <security@finvero.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Audit log export: residency/retention edge cases

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. A few follow-ups from our legal and security teams after the compliance review:

- Can Redwood produce an on-demand export that covers events outside the normal retention window (e.g., restore logs older than 90 days) for customers in a legal hold? If so, what are the limits and lead times?
- For EU tenants, exports must not cross regions unless explicitly authorized. Can you confirm what controls exist to pin an export to an EU-only destination (and what evidence you provide)?
- Do exports include deletion/tombstone markers and chain-of-custody metadata (checksums, job IDs, who requested the export)?
- Preferred formats: our infra prefers parquet or ndjson; do you support both and can you include schema documentation?

We'd also like a short manifest we can use to validate an incoming export. Can you share an example and the expected SLA for producing a one-off export?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

--
Alice Nguyen
Security Lead, Finvero
alice@finvero.com
[attachment: export_manifest_request.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finvero.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log export: residency/retention edge cases

Hi Alice — thanks, and hi team (Jonas, Ben) — looping you in for the technical answers. Quick answers up front, then a short plan: 

- On-demand exports for data beyond the default retention: possible, with caveats. For Hosted customers we can produce ad-hoc extracts up to 180 days *if* the tenant's backing storage still holds archived chunks; beyond that, a recovery from warm cold-storage may be required and lead times increase to 3–5 business days. For Dedicated/Private, retention is configurable by contract and can be extended programmatically.

- EU-only exports: we can stage the export inside a customer-provided EU S3 bucket (preferred) or Redwood can stage within our EU region and provide a signed transfer link. We supply an export manifest that contains region and residency assertions and will sign the manifest (SHA256) for chain-of-custody.

- Deletion markers: exports include event-level metadata by default (timestamp, actor, event_type, tenant_id, object_id). Tombstone/deletion flag is included for audit logs; for access logs we can optionally include a "deleted:true" flag or omit deleted records if required.

- Formats: we support ndjson and parquet for bulk exports; CSV is available for small slices. Schema docs will be attached.

Plan:
1) I'll draft the export manifest template and checklist (attached).
2) Jonas will outline the technical packaging (chunking, compression, checksums).
3) We'll confirm a delivery mechanism (your EU bucket vs Redwood staging).

Can you confirm whether Finvero requires the export to include raw KV cache traces or only audit/access events? Also confirm your preferred destination (Finvero bucket vs Redwood EU staging).

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)
marissa@redwood.com
[attachment: export_manifest_template.csv]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@finvero.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log export: residency/retention edge cases

On Thu, Mar 1, 2028 at 09:06, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Formats: we support ndjson and parquet for bulk exports; CSV is available for small slices.
>
Additional technical notes from infra: 

- Packaging: exports are produced as gzipped chunks (parquet.gz or ndjson.gz) ~100–500MB per chunk by default; we can tune chunk size. Each chunk has an associated SHA256 checksum in the manifest.
- Delivery: presigned S3 PUT to customer bucket (recommended), or we can stage and provide presigned GET URLs for download. Presigned URL TTL defaults to 48 hours but can be extended for special cases.
- Schema & redaction: we emit tenant_id, event_ts, event_type, object_id, actor_id (hashed if requested), and metadata.json fields. PII redaction is a step in the export pipeline—if you require it, we run redaction and mark fields in the manifest.
- Retention vs recovery: if requested range crosses the configured retention boundary (e.g., you ask for months 1–6 but default retention is 90 days) and archive exists, job status = "delayed-rehydrate" while we pull from cold store. Expect 24–72 hours for small jobs, 3–5 days for large historical pulls.

I'll attach a short s3 delivery steps stub and example manifest.

-Jonas

[attachment: s3-delivery-steps.txt]

From: Finvero Security <security@finvero.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@finvero.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log export: residency/retention edge cases

Marissa / Jonas,

Thanks, useful. A couple of clarifications before we sign off on a test export: 

- We need explicit confirmation that the manifest will include a job requestor identifier (email) and a signed SHA256 checksum for each chunk.
- Does the export include application-level traces (KV/cache activity) or only audit/access events? We specifically need to know whether cache hits/misses are captured in the export (our incident team wants traces for reproducing timeline).
- Chain-of-custody: if Redwood stages the export in your EU region, do you provide logs proving the objects never left the region (object-level region props / storage-class audit)?

Also, please attach one short example manifest (with placeholder checksums) so we can validate parsing on our side.

-Alice

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Finvero Security <security@finvero.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@finvero.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit log export: residency/retention edge cases

Hi Alice — short confirmation and next steps: 

- Manifest: yes, each chunk will have SHA256 and a job_requestor field populated with the requester email. We'll include checksums and job_id in the top-level manifest and sign the manifest with our export key. Example manifest attached.
- Cache traces: not included by default for exports (we treat KV cache traces as ephemeral internal telemetry). If you need cache-level traces for an incident, we can produce them under a separate request (requires Dedicated/Private or a signed data-sharing agreement). That request is handled as an elevated forensics job and has a 3–5 day lead time.
- Region proof: when we stage to our EU bucket we attach the storage object metadata and a signed transfer manifest proving the objects remained in the EU region; we can also provide a transfer log (object-level timestamps and storage-class history).

Next steps: if Finvero confirms destination (preferred: your EU S3 bucket with a short test prefix), we'll open ticket FIN-4821, schedule a short handoff call, and run a small pilot export (last 7 days) within 48 hours. For the pilot we'll provide: example manifest, checksums, and a CSV mapping file for schema.

Attached: export_manifest_template.csv, export-checklist.pdf

Thanks and happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Regards,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
